newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex sees jump in 1997 investment, higher output.
newsitem.headline: Pemex sees jump in 1997 investment, higher output.

text.p: State oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) plans to increase investment spending sharply in 1997, mainly in its exploration and production division, according to corporation documents released by Pemex chairman Adrian Lajous Wednesday.

The documents, handed to reporters as Pemex released third quarter results, showed plans to boost total investment spending by 67 percent to $5.916 billion next year. Pemex said $4.069 billion of that total would be spent on exploration and production.
The documents also said Pemex planned to increase crude output next year to 3.08 million barrels per day (bpd), a rise of eight percent from this year's projected average of 2.86 million bpd.
Natural gas output is also set to rise next year to 4.545 billion cubic feet per day (cfd), eight percent more than this year's projected average of 4.198 billion cfd.
Pemex also said its nine-month pretax consolidated profit this year was $15.651 billion, up 25 percent on the same period a year ago.
